generatedProse.concept-context: Whatever you study, excelling means more than a strong mark in your modules. Alongside the grade sits your growth as a thinker: becoming more curious about the questions your subject asks, more careful with evidence, and more independent in how you judge it. A student who earns a good grade and also becomes a sharper, more questioning learner has excelled more fully than one who earns the grade alone.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two students on the same first-year module.

Student A has one aim: the highest mark possible. Student A learns exactly what the marker wants, revises precisely that, and is pleased with a strong grade. The mark is real, but nothing else has changed. Student A is no more curious about the subject than before, and has little interest in the ideas beyond the assessment. This is success measured only as academic performance.

Student B wants to do well too, but also wants to understand the subject and become a better thinker. Student B reads around the topic, follows up ideas that are not strictly needed for the mark, and finishes more confident and more interested than before. The grade is good, and growth has happened as well. This is excelling: academic performance and personal development together.

Both students passed well. Only Student B treated the module as a chance to grow, not just a grade to earn.
generatedProse.summary: Excelling means more than a high mark. Success has two sides: academic performance, the grades and skills, and personal development, the way you grow as a thinker through your studies. Excelling is a mindset you bring, not a fixed trait. You can now define excelling in this fuller way and recognise the mindset behind it. The next lesson looks at the growth mindset and self-belief that make it possible.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Student B's approach closer to excelling?

items.text: Student B earned a good grade and also grew more confident and interested in the subject.
Student B earned a higher grade than Student A did.
Student B spent far longer on the module than Student A did.
Student B focused only on what the marker wanted.

feedback.correct: That's right. Student B scored well and grew as a thinker, which is excelling.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Student B gained beyond the grade.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Student B excelled by growing in confidence and interest as well as scoring well, not because of a higher grade or more time.
